talks.title: Bypass 101
talks.teaser: An introduction to mechanical lock bypass principles, latch slipping, shimming, and non-destructive physical entry methods.
talks.summary:
In this instructional demonstration from the DEF CON Safe Mode Lock Bypass Village, Karen presents "Bypass 101," a beginner-friendly introduction to non-destructive physical bypass techniques that circumvent door access controls without manipulating internal lock cylinders. Opening at 00:01, Karen introduces the fundamental principles of physical security auditing.

At 07:00, she demonstrates the deployment of under-the-door bypass tools, illustrating how a specialized wire armature can be slipped beneath commercial exterior doors to hook and pull internal lever handles from the outside. At 14:00, she analyzes exterior hinge vulnerabilities, demonstrating how exposed hinge pins and loose door gaps can be exploited using simple shims.

At 21:00 and 28:01, Karen reviews stairwell and elevator access controls, explaining how elevator hacking techniques bypass floor lockouts and demonstrating how attendees can fabricate their own custom bypass tools for physical penetration testing engagements. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Alarms and Access Controlled Doors
talks.teaser: Examines sensor mechanisms, request-to-exit bypasses, and alarm defeat techniques on commercial access-controlled doors.
talks.summary:
Bill Graydon delivers a comprehensive technical overview of electronic access control systems (ACS) and intrusion detection systems (IDS), breaking down the hardware architecture, sensor mechanics, and bypass methodologies utilized during physical security assessments [00:00]. Graydon examines the standard components of secure portals, including magnetic contact switches (reed switches), request-to-exit (REX) passive infrared (PIR) motion detectors, push buttons, push crash bars, electric strikes, and electromagnetic locks (maglocks) [06:21].

The presentation explores both physical and electronic attack vectors against door sensing circuits. Graydon illustrates how attackers defeat magnetic door contacts using strong external neodymium magnets to simulate a closed door while physically opening it [13:06]. He details how alarm panels monitor sensor wiring using supervised loops with End-of-Line (EOL) resistors, explaining how single and double EOL resistor circuits detect line tampering (shorts and opens) and how pen-testers defeat supervision by measuring and bridging matching resistances onto the line [19:47]. He also addresses vulnerabilities in wireless sensors, comparing AM and FM transmission characteristics and jamming resilience [26:45].

Graydon covers bypasses against egress detection hardware, including using compressed air or thermal devices to activate REX sensors, manipulating crash bars using under-the-door tools, and exploiting maglock mechanical installations [33:42]. He reviews intrusion alarm state machines (Armed, Disarmed, Alarm) [40:28] and PIR sensor beam patterns, noting blind spots directly below sensors and along perpendicular lines of sight [47:01]. The session concludes with recommendations for physical defenders, emphasizing tamper-resistant conduit, balanced magnetic switches (BMS), and hardened egress controls.
